'''Business and economy'''
*[[Argentine debt restructuring]]
**Argentine minister of economy [[Martín Guzmán]] warns that the [[International Monetary Fund]] will "lose legitimacy" if it fails in negotiations with the country, with Guzmán citing his country's growth of nearly 10 percent as an argument. [https://www.ambito.com/economia/fmi/martin-guzman-el-puede-perder-legitimidad-si-argentina-se-desestabiliza-n5353354 (Ámbito)]
*[[Puerto Rican government-debt crisis]]
**A [[United States federal judge|federal judge]] signs a plan to [[economic restructuring|restructure]] [[Puerto Rico]]'s economy, allowing it to start repaying [[government debt|debt]] to [[creditors]] and lifting it out of [[bankruptcy]]. [https://apnews.com/article/business-caribbean-puerto-rico-bcc3dd61544e8b0a401bbd6567c04da6 (AP News)]
*[[Microsoft]] announces that it will acquire gaming company [[Activision Blizzard]] for $68.7 billion. If the acquisition is successful, Activision Blizzard will become part of [[Xbox Game Studios]], which will become the world's third-largest gaming company behind [[Tencent]] and [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/microsoft-buy-activision-blizzard-deal-687-billion-2022-01-18/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Antananarivo floods]]
**At least ten people are killed by floods in [[Antananarivo]], [[Madagascar]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2022/01/18/10-killed-by-floods-in-madagascar/ (Africanews)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] orders the culling of 2,000 small animals, such as [[hamster]]s, [[chinchilla]]s and [[rabbit]]s, closes pet shops, and sends 100 people to a [[quarantine]] camp after nearly a dozen hamsters imported from the [[Netherlands]] and sold at Little Boss pet shop were infected with the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] which also spread to two people. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-01-18/hong-kong-goes-on-hamster-crackdown-after-shock-delta-flareup (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] reports a record 32,197 new [[COVID-19]] cases in the past 24 hours. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220118/p2g/00m/0na/057000c (''The Mainichi'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] reports a record 10,258 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 972,198. [https://www.laprensalatina.com/nepal-registers-highest-single-day-covid-spike-as-fresh-wave-intensifies/ (La Prensa Latina)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Bulgaria]] reports a record 9,996 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 830,604. [http://www.bta.bg/en/c/DF/id/2556098 (Bulgarian Press Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports a record 464,769 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/france-reports-all-time-high-for-new-coronavirus-cases/2478863 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Second Deputy Prime Minister of Spain]] [[Yolanda Díaz]] and [[Ministry of Science (Spain)|Minister of Science and Innovation]] [[Diana Morant]] both test positive for COVID-19. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/economia/20220118/yolanda-diaz-diana-morant-comunica-13116434 (''El Periódico'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City]]
****The [[Cardinal Secretary of State]] [[Pietro Parolin]] and his deputy [[Edgar Peña Parra]] both test positive for COVID-19. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/01/18/world/europe/pope-francis-coronavirus-parolin-pena-parra.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
****[[Brazil]] reports a record 137,102 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 23,211,894. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-reports-351-covid-19-deaths-highest-daily-toll-since-nov-17-ministry-2022-01-18/ (Reuters)]

**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]

**[[COVID-19 drug development]]
***[[Merck & Co.]] and its partner [[Ridgeback Biotherapeutics]] sign an agreement with [[UNICEF]] to distribute up to 3 million courses of their COVID-19 antiviral pill [[molnupiravir]] to 100 low and middle-income countries in the first half of the year.
